basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 12.' and it opens 'Vers. 12. Mulier, quam dedisti. Quasi in hoc Deum infamaret, qui ei dederat per quam'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 12. Mulier, quam dedisti. Quasi in hoc Deum infamaret, qui ei dederat per quam deceptus fuerat. Similiter et mulier interrogata in serpentem reflexit culpam, dicens: Serpens decepit me. Quo morbo laborat usque hodie humanum genus. Denique serpens non interrogatur, quia diabolus, qui per serpentem locutus fuerat, irrecuperabiliter deliquerat. Et bene Adam primo interrogatur cui praeceptum dederat Deus, quod praeceptum per virum venit ad mulierem: | sicut e contra per serpentem peccatum venit ad mulierem, et per mulierem ad virum.
